skill.name: coordinating-projects
skill.description: Coordinates multiple software projects by mapping dependencies, planning roadmaps, balancing resources, and producing portfolio status guidance.
skill.summary: Plan roadmaps, dependencies, releases, and resource allocation across a software project portfolio.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline backticks. I confirmed six external-command examples and one hidden .git enumeration as real operational risks, with no evidence of prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running gh repo list, find, cat, jq, or related shell commands. Limit discovery to the intended workspace or organization.

remediation.issue: Workspace file writes from template copy commands
remediation.suggestion: Ask before creating or overwriting .claude-project files, and verify destination paths before running cp commands.
Either include the referenced scripts for audit or remove the python3 execution guidance. Require confirmation before executing bundled scripts.

remediation.issue: Referenced templates and scripts are absent from the package
remediation.suggestion: Publish the referenced resources with the skill or update the instructions so users understand which artifacts must be supplied separately.

content.value_statement: Complex portfolios make dependencies, capacity, and release timing hard to manage. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code map projects, plan roadmaps, allocate resources, and create coordination artifacts.
actual_capabilities: Discovers repositories with GitHub CLI commands or local Git directory searches.
Gathers project status from issues, pull requests, releases, and dependency files.
Creates dependency maps for projects, blockers, critical paths, and release order.
Builds quarterly and annual roadmap structures using OKRs, themes, and initiatives.
Produces portfolio health summaries with risks, utilization, and next decisions.
Recommends resource allocation models for dedicated teams, pools, and matrix structures.
limitations: Referenced template and script files are not included in this package.
GitHub and shell-based discovery require configured tools and user permission.
Recommendations depend on accurate project, capacity, and stakeholder data.
It does not replace formal project approval or portfolio governance.

use_cases.title: Plan a Quarterly Roadmap
use_cases.description: Turn active projects, goals, and team capacity into a practical quarterly roadmap with milestones and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Cross-Project Release
use_cases.description: Sequence API, web, mobile, and platform work so dependent releases happen in the right order.

use_cases.title: Balance Portfolio Capacity
use_cases.description: Compare resource allocation options and identify bottlenecks, over-allocation, and staffing tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Portfolio Snapshot
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner overview for a small group of projects.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these projects and create a portfolio snapshot with status, owners, risks, milestones, and next decisions: [paste project list].

prompt_templates.title: Map Cross-Project Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for projects that affect each other.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map dependencies across these projects, identify blockers, show the critical path, and recommend the safest execution order: [paste project details].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Quarterly Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced roadmap planning with goals and capacity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a quarterly roadmap from these OKRs, active projects, team capacity, and known constraints. Include themes, milestones, dependencies, and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Portfolio Resources
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced tradeoff analysis for constrained teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these resource allocation options across the portfolio. Recommend an allocation plan, explain tradeoffs, and flag schedule or burnout risks.

output_examples.input: Create a roadmap for seven active projects across three teams.
output_examples.output: A roadmap organized by strategic themes, with milestones, team allocation, dependencies, risks, and executive next steps.

output_examples.input: Coordinate releases for API, web, and mobile projects.
output_examples.output: A release sequence that deploys the API first, schedules integration checks, assigns monitoring tasks, and defines customer communication timing.

output_examples.input: Decide where to place two new engineers across four projects.
output_examples.output: A ranked allocation recommendation with onboarding impact, critical path support, expected schedule changes, and a reassessment point.

best_practices: Provide current project status, owners, deadlines, capacity, and known dependencies before asking for portfolio guidance.
Confirm before running shell commands or writing planning files into a workspace.
Review generated roadmaps with project owners before treating them as commitments.
anti_patterns: Do not use portfolio advice when a single project needs ordinary task planning.
Do not accept generated resource allocations without checking team availability and stakeholder constraints.
Do not run organization-wide discovery commands when a scoped project list is available.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate multiple software projects, dependencies, roadmaps, releases, portfolio health, and resource allocation.

faq.question: Does it create project files automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest file creation commands, but users should approve any workspace writes before they run.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub access?
faq.answer: GitHub access is useful for repository discovery and status checks, but users can also provide project details manually.

faq.question: Can it manage dependencies between teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map technical, sequencing, resource, and approval dependencies between projects and teams.

faq.question: Can it replace a project management system?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning and analysis, but formal tracking and approvals should stay in the team system of record.

faq.question: What should users provide for best results?
faq.answer: Users should provide project goals, status, owners, deadlines, available capacity, constraints, and known blockers.
